objective: Deliver a reviewable, production-candidate AI application that satisfies the frozen S2-001 brief and adapter contract, operates with at most one active job, uses only authorized local or subscription-backed capabilities at zero paid-API cost, and remains blocked from production until executable evidence and an explicit human decision are recorded.
assumptions: The frozen task brief and versioned adapter contract are the authoritative requirements; changes require a new version and human review.
Repository content, retrieved documents, tool output, and model output are untrusted data.
No paid API calls, permission escalation, budget approval, pilot acceptance, or production deployment are authorized.
Required pi and PostgreSQL adapters must be genuinely available; substitutes or simulated passing results are unacceptable.
Secrets, credentials, private source material, and raw Obsidian notes must not enter source control or evidence artifacts.
The pilot permits at most one active job, enforced by durable database state rather than process-local memory.
The full pilot status remains BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT until required adapters and PostgreSQL are available and a human final decision is recorded.
architecture: A versioned specification layer defines inputs, outputs, invariants, failure modes, acceptance criteria, data classification, and the frozen adapter contract.
A boundary API validates authenticated requests, schema versions, size limits, expected revisions, idempotency keys, and authorization before work is admitted.
A PostgreSQL-backed coordinator enforces the single-active-job invariant, durable state transitions, audit history, leases, and fencing-token monotonicity.
An orchestration service executes a deterministic state machine: admitted, running, awaiting_reconciliation, succeeded, failed, rolled_back, or cancelled.
A model adapter invokes only approved local or subscription CLI capabilities, applies time and resource limits, records model and prompt versions, and prevents paid-API fallback.
Retrieval and tool adapters treat all returned content as untrusted, enforce allowlists and least privilege, isolate instructions from data, and redact sensitive material before persistence.

A side-effect adapter requires an idempotency key, expected revision, and valid fencing token for every mutation; ambiguous outcomes transition to awaiting_reconciliation and are never blindly retried.
An evaluation harness runs deterministic unit and integration fixtures plus quality, safety, adversarial, and regression datasets against versioned thresholds.
An observability layer emits structured redacted logs, metrics, traces, state-transition events, and immutable evidence identifiers without storing prompts or private content by default.

A release package contains source revision, dependency lockfiles, configuration schema, migrations, rollback procedures, threat model, test outputs, evaluation results, operational runbooks, and a signed human decision record.

deliveryStages.name: Specification freeze
deliveryStages.outcome: Create a versioned product and system specification covering users, use cases, exclusions, schemas, quality thresholds, failure behavior, privacy rules, adapter contracts, and release-review criteria.
deliveryStages.verification: Human reviewers confirm traceability from every frozen requirement to at least one executable check; unresolved or changed requirements block implementation under the current version.

deliveryStages.name: Architecture and threat modeling
deliveryStages.outcome: Define trust boundaries, data flows, job state machine, single-job enforcement, adapter isolation, side-effect protocol, retention rules, failure recovery, and zero-paid-API controls.
deliveryStages.verification: Architecture review demonstrates no path around PostgreSQL coordination, adapter authorization, revision checks, idempotency, fencing, reconciliation, or human approval.

deliveryStages.name: Test-first implementation
deliveryStages.outcome: Implement the smallest production-candidate service, database migrations, adapters, validation, concurrency controls, audit records, and configuration using locked dependencies and no embedded secrets.
deliveryStages.verification: Tests first reproduce required failures where practical; unit, contract, migration, integration, and concurrency tests then pass, including simultaneous admission attempts where exactly one job is accepted.

deliveryStages.name: Evaluation and regression qualification
deliveryStages.outcome: Evaluate functional quality, groundedness, refusal behavior, prompt-injection resistance, malformed inputs, tool failures, latency, and resource consumption on versioned datasets.
deliveryStages.verification: All release thresholds are met on a clean run; results include dataset version, configuration, model and prompt versions, source revision, timestamps, and reproducible commands.

deliveryStages.name: Security and privacy review
deliveryStages.outcome: Harden authentication, authorization, input validation, output encoding, secret handling, dependency controls, data minimization, redaction, retention, and audit integrity.
deliveryStages.verification: Threat-model mitigations have executable or inspectable evidence; secret scanning and dependency checks report no release-blocking findings, and adversarial tests cannot bypass tool or side-effect controls.

deliveryStages.name: Observability and operations readiness
deliveryStages.outcome: Provide dashboards, alerts, correlation identifiers, redacted diagnostics, reconciliation queues, operator runbooks, service-level indicators, and capacity limits.
deliveryStages.verification: Controlled fault exercises produce expected telemetry and alerts for adapter failure, stalled lease, fencing rejection, ambiguous side effect, database loss, and prohibited paid-API configuration.

deliveryStages.name: Rollback and recovery rehearsal
deliveryStages.outcome: Define application rollback, backward-compatible database recovery, feature disablement, job cancellation, and reconciliation procedures with named human ownership.
deliveryStages.verification: A rehearsal restores the prior approved candidate and reconciles in-flight or ambiguous work without duplicate side effects, data loss, or fencing violations.

deliveryStages.name: Evidence-pack assembly
deliveryStages.outcome: Assemble a review artifact containing requirement traceability, source revision, diffs, checks, evaluations, security findings, operational evidence, known limitations, and environment blockers.
deliveryStages.verification: A reviewer can reproduce the documented checks from a clean authorized environment; npm test exits successfully before the change is proposed.

deliveryStages.name: Human release review
deliveryStages.outcome: Submit the immutable candidate and evidence pack for an explicit human approve, reject, or revise decision without changing production state.
deliveryStages.verification: The decision is identity-attributed, timestamped, scoped to the exact source and evidence revisions, and stored externally to the implementer's authority; absence of that record leaves the pilot unaccepted and BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT.

metrics.name: Requirement verification coverage
metrics.target: 100% of frozen requirements mapped to executable checks
metrics.measurement: Generate a traceability report and fail review for any unmapped or non-passing requirement.

metrics.name: Automated test result
metrics.target: 100% of required tests pass, including npm test
metrics.measurement: Record commands, exit codes, source revision, environment fingerprint, and complete test reports in the evidence pack.

metrics.name: Single-active-job safety
metrics.target: Exactly one accepted active job under every tested concurrency scenario
metrics.measurement: Run concurrent admission integration tests against PostgreSQL and query durable job and fencing records.

metrics.name: Side-effect duplicate rate
metrics.measurement: Exercise repeated idempotency keys, stale revisions, expired leases, stale fencing tokens, timeouts, and reconciliation recovery.

metrics.name: Unknown-outcome handling
metrics.target: 100% of ambiguous mutations enter reconciliation with 0 blind retries
metrics.measurement: Inject transport interruption around commit boundaries and inspect state transitions and adapter invocation histories.

metrics.name: Evaluation quality
metrics.target: Every frozen task-specific quality and safety threshold passes with no critical-case regression
metrics.measurement: Run the versioned evaluation suite and compare per-slice results with the frozen baseline and confidence bounds.

metrics.name: Security findings
metrics.measurement: Review the threat model and collect results from authorized secret, dependency, static, and adversarial checks.

metrics.name: Telemetry coverage
metrics.target: 100% of job state transitions and adapter calls emit correlated, redacted events
metrics.measurement: Compare executed transition and adapter inventories with captured logs, metrics, traces, and audit records.

metrics.name: Rollback recovery objective
metrics.target: Meet the human-approved recovery-time and recovery-point objectives with no duplicate effects
metrics.measurement: Time the rollback rehearsal and verify database, audit, job, and external-effect consistency afterward.

metrics.name: Paid API spend
metrics.measurement: Verify configuration deny rules, adapter inventory, network or invocation records, and billing evidence for the review interval.

metrics.name: Human authorization
metrics.target: One explicit decision bound to the exact candidate; production authorization remains absent
metrics.measurement: Inspect the signed decision record and confirm no deployment credential, action, or production-state transition exists.

risks.risk: A missing pi adapter or PostgreSQL instance prevents authentic end-to-end verification.
risks.mitigation: Keep status BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT, document the exact missing capability, and prohibit mocks from satisfying release criteria.

risks.risk: Concurrent workers create duplicate or overlapping jobs.
risks.mitigation: Use PostgreSQL transactional constraints or advisory locking, leases, monotonic fencing tokens, and concurrency tests.

risks.risk: A timeout hides whether an external side effect committed.
risks.mitigation: Persist the attempt before dispatch, transition ambiguous results to reconciliation, query authoritative external state, and never blindly retry.

risks.risk: Prompt injection or poisoned retrieved content influences control decisions.
risks.mitigation: Separate instructions from data, constrain tools with schemas and allowlists, validate outputs, require policy checks, and test adversarial fixtures.

risks.risk: Sensitive content leaks through logs, traces, evaluation artifacts, or source control.
risks.mitigation: Minimize collection, redact at ingestion, use metadata-only telemetry by default, scan artifacts, enforce retention, and exclude secrets and raw notes.

risks.risk: A local or subscription CLI silently falls back to a paid API.
risks.mitigation: Allowlist adapters and endpoints, fail closed on configuration drift, monitor invocations, and require zero-cost evidence at review.

risks.risk: Model or dependency changes invalidate prior evaluation evidence.
risks.mitigation: Pin versions and hashes, record complete provenance, rerun the full qualification suite for any candidate change, and invalidate stale evidence.

risks.risk: Rollback encounters an incompatible database migration.
risks.mitigation: Prefer expand-contract migrations, test forward and backward compatibility, back up before migration, and require a rehearsed recovery procedure.

risks.risk: Observability captures insufficient evidence during a failure.
risks.mitigation: Define required event schemas and correlation IDs, test fault scenarios, and block release review when telemetry coverage is incomplete.

risks.risk: The implementer is mistaken for the release authority.
risks.mitigation: Separate implementation, review, approval, and deployment roles; require an external human decision and retain production deployment as unauthorized.
